summary.goal: Add a generic multi-plan execution layer to Forge that accepts a pre-computed DAG of plan references organized into tiers, executes them as coordinated runs tier-by-tier, and tracks aggregate build state. Any client (Planner, testbench, CLI) can submit a build request — Forge doesn't care about the source, it just executes.
in_scope: Build entity with tier-based execution model
Tier-by-tier execution: complete tier N before starting tier N+1
Parallel execution within tiers (up to concurrency limit)
Build-level pause/resume/cancel propagating to child runs
Failure handling: failed run blocks dependent tiers, siblings continue
Incremental builds: skip plans with recent successful completions
Plan fetching via PlannerClient at execution time (not at proposal time)
out_of_scope: Dependency graph resolution (that's Planner's job — Forge receives pre-computed tiers)
Build proposal/analysis (Planner computes this by querying Forge for run history)
UI for builds (separate feature in planner-ui)
Plan approval workflow (plans must be approved before build)
Cross-build coordination (running build A and build B simultaneously with shared state)

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /api/forge/builds accepts tiers of plan_ids and creates a build with child runs
Build executes tier 0 runs immediately, waits for all to complete before advancing to tier 1
Within a tier, runs execute in parallel up to the configured concurrency limit
If a run in tier N fails, tier N+1 is blocked but other tier N runs continue to completion
Build-level pause stops scheduling new runs and pauses in-progress runs
Build-level cancel cancels all in-progress and queued runs
GET /api/forge/builds/:id returns build status with per-tier, per-run progress
GET /api/forge/builds/:id/events streams SSE events for build-level state changes
Builds with skip_completed=true skip plans that have a recent successful run
A single-plan build (1 tier, 1 plan) works identically to the existing POST /runs flow
Build correctly fetches each plan from Planner via PlannerClient before creating runs

observations: Forge is intentionally a single-plan executor — builds add a layer ABOVE runs, not replacing them
The existing orchestrator handles tasks within a run; the build coordinator handles runs within a build
sub_plan_id support in orchestrator is hierarchical (parent embeds child) — builds are lateral (independent plans coordinated)
Test mode (TestExecutor) should work with builds — each run in the build uses test execution
PlannerClient already exists and can fetch plans — builds just call it per plan in each tier
The build coordinator is conceptually similar to the orchestrator but at a higher level of abstraction
Builds are ephemeral execution state — they don't need versioning or approval (that's the plans themselves)
questions: Should builds support 'retry tier' (re-run all failed runs in a tier)?
What happens if a plan was modified between proposal and execution? Use version pinning?
Should the concurrency limit be per-tier or per-build?

architect.pattern: Forge owns build execution state, Planner owns build resolution/proposal
architect.rationale: Build is execution state (runs, progress, failures). Keeping it in forge.db avoids cross-DB sync. Makes Forge's builds API generically usable by any client.
architect.execution_model: Tier-based DAG: tiers execute sequentially, plans within a tier execute in parallel. Same model as CI/CD pipeline stages.
architect.storage: Two new tables in forge.db: builds (build state) and build_runs (maps runs to builds with tier info)
architect.relationship_to_runs: A build creates N runs. Each run is a standard Forge run. The build coordinator monitors and advances tiers.
